title: 1:1 with Maya

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Hey Maya, thanks for making time.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Grab a coffee first, or should we just dive in?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: I'm good, let's dive in, I've got a hard stop at eleven for a supplier call.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Works for me.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: How's the calibration algorithm work going?

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Last I heard you were chasing that offset drift on the humidity channel.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: We found it, actually.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: It wasn't the sensor, it was our reference temperature compensation table, it was built off the old C-series thermistor curve and the new batch uses a slightly different part with a steeper resistance curve at high humidity.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Interesting, so it's been silently wrong for how long?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Hard to say exactly, but at least since the rev B boards started shipping in July.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: The drift is small, under half a percent, but it compounds over a long unattended run, so it adds up more than you'd expect.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Did it show up in any field complaints?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: One, from Solenne Biolabs.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: They flagged some readings drifting over a forty-eight hour unattended run in one of their incubators.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: I didn't connect it to the thermistor curve until I dug into it properly this week.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Good catch.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: What's the fix, a new lookup table?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Yeah, I've got a corrected table built from bench data on twelve units.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: I just need Tomas or Greta to help me validate it against a fresh batch before we ship it as a firmware patch.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Is that something we fold into the Q4 release, or does it need to go out sooner?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Sooner, honestly, given it's a live field issue affecting a named customer.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Maybe a small point release ahead of the main Q4 push, something we can turn around in a week or two.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Let's do that.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: I'll make sure someone has bandwidth for it this week, I know Tomas is also pulled onto the sleep mode work and Greta's mid-sweep on her own calibration harness.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: That would help a lot.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: I've been a bit stretched trying to cover the fix on top of catching up from yesterday's steerco.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: How did steerco go?

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: I only caught the tail end of the recap in the channel.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Mostly fine, my cost-per-unit numbers for the Aegis line held up under questioning, though Rafael flagged the enclosure tooling lead time again, so there's some risk hanging over the launch date that isn't really firmware's to solve.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Anything from it that lands on your desk directly?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Just a note to keep an eye on the antenna cutout dimensions if the enclosure tooling changes, since we calibrated the BLE diagnostic mode's range testing against the current prototype.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: I'll flag it to Tomas and Inès too.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Let's shift gears a bit.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: I wanted to talk about where you see yourself going here, beyond the immediate firmware work.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: I've been thinking about that too, actually, more than usual lately.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: I'd like to move into more of a lead role on the sensor firmware side, less individual contributor work, more owning the roadmap and mentoring the rest of the team.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: That tracks with what I've been seeing.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: You've basically been doing a lot of that informally already, especially with Inès on the hardware side and now with Greta ramping up.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Yeah, I like working with both of them.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Inès picks things up fast, she just needs someone pointing her at the right problem instead of the loudest one.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Greta's still finding her feet but she asks good questions.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: I think there's a real case for making that formal, a firmware team lead role covering the Vantage line now and Aegis once that ships.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Would you want to put together a short proposal, what it would look like, staffing, how you'd split your time between leading and doing?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: I'd like that, yeah.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Can I have until next Friday?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: I want to actually think it through rather than dash something off before my supplier call.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Perfect, let's make that the action item.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: On my side, I want to give you some feedback on the quarter, is now a good time for that?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Sure, go ahead.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Overall really strong.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: The calibration accuracy work you did in August moved the needle on our biggest recurring customer complaint, and you've been a steady hand keeping Tomas and Inès pointed in the right direction without me having to referee anything between them.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Good to hear.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: It didn't always feel that smooth from the inside, there were a couple of weeks in August where I felt like I was just triaging fires.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: That's fair, and it didn't show externally, which is its own skill.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: The one growth area I'd flag, and it ties into the lead conversation, is writing more of this down.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: A lot of what you know about the calibration pipeline lives only in your head, and that's a risk if you're out sick, on vacation, or busy leading instead of doing.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: That's fair, I know the calibration doc is stale, I keep meaning to get to it and something else always jumps the queue.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: No rush on all of it at once, but maybe that becomes part of the lead proposal too, a plan for getting the tribal knowledge written down as you delegate pieces of the work to Inès and Greta.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Makes sense, I'll fold that into the proposal, maybe frame it as a documentation sprint once the calibration patch ships.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: How are you doing otherwise, workload-wise?

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: You mentioned being stretched a minute ago.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Honestly, okay, not burnt out, just busy.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: I turned down a sensor conference in October because the timing was bad with the Q4 release crunch, but I might try to go to the spring one instead if the schedule allows.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Let's plan for that now, put it on the calendar so it doesn't get eaten by whatever's on fire in March.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: I'd rather protect it in advance than have you cancel again.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Deal, I'll send you the dates.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: While we're on logistics, how's the relationship with the manufacturing side going, specifically Rafael's team?

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: You mentioned the yield data dependency a minute ago.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: It's generally good, he's responsive, it's more that his team is stretched thin right now with the Aegis tooling work, so anything I need from them queues up behind the higher priority stuff.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Is that something I should raise with him directly, or would that undercut you?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: I don't think you need to yet, it's manageable, I just wanted you to have the context in case it becomes a pattern before the Aegis launch.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Appreciated, keep me posted if it gets worse.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Let's go back to the calibration patch for a second, what does the validation plan actually look like once you've got the corrected lookup table?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: The plan is to flash it to twelve bench units, six from the batch that shipped to Solenne and six from an earlier batch, and run a seventy-two hour soak at three humidity setpoints, forty percent, sixty percent, and eighty-five percent.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: If the drift stays under a tenth of a percent across all eighteen setpoint-unit combinations, I'm comfortable shipping it.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Seventy-two hours is a long soak for a point release, will that push the timeline past what you told Solenne?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: It's tight but doable if we start the soak by Wednesday.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: I already told their support contact we're targeting a patch by the end of next week, so there's a little slack built in.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Good, and who's actually running the soak, is that you or can you hand it off?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: I'd like to hand the mechanics of it to Greta, actually, partly because it's good experience for her and partly because it frees me up now that steerco's behind us.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: I'd still review the data before we ship anything.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: That's a nice fit with the lead conversation we just had, delegating the execution while you keep ownership of the decision.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Exactly, that's sort of what made me think about it in the first place.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Watching myself hand this off made the whole lead-role idea feel less abstract.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: How is Greta doing generally, since you're closer to her day to day work than I am?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: She's doing well.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: She's still building intuition for which test failures are real versus flaky infrastructure, but her instincts are good and she asks before guessing, which I'd rather have than the opposite.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Any specific support she needs that I should know about?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Mostly just more exposure to the calibration pipeline end to end, right now she only sees her slice of it.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Once the lead role is real I'd like to rotate her through a full calibration cycle so she understands why the reference tables matter, not just how to run the harness.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: That's a good plan, put it in the proposal as part of the ramp plan for her, it'll help me understand headcount implications too.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Will do.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: One more thing on the postmortem side, do you want a short writeup on the humidity drift issue for the incident log, or is a mention in the calibration doc enough?

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Let's do a short writeup, even a page.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: It's the kind of thing that's useful the next time someone hits a weird drift and searches for it, and it's good practice for the documentation habit we just talked about.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Fair, I'll draft it after the soak test finishes so I can include the actual before-and-after numbers rather than just the theory.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Perfect.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Last thing before we wrap, how's your team's onboarding process feeling now that Greta's a few months in?

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Anything you'd change for the next hire?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: I'd give the next person a smaller first project.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Greta's first task was the calibration harness rewrite, which was probably too big, it took her three weeks to feel confident touching it.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Something scoped to a week would build confidence faster.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Good feedback, I'll keep that in mind, we might be hiring again once Aegis firmware ramps up in Q1.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: That would be good timing, actually, since by then I'd have more bandwidth to onboard someone properly instead of doing it in the gaps.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Noted.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Let's talk logistics on the lead role for a second, since I know the mechanics matter to you.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Once you send me the proposal, I'll take it to Sun and to leadership review, and realistically that's a two to three week cycle before anything's official.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: That timeline's fine, I wasn't expecting it to be instant.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Does the title change come with a comp conversation too, or is that a separate process?

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Separate process, but I'll flag it at the same time so they're not sequential, comp review usually follows within a cycle of a title change, not months later.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: I'll push for that explicitly.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Appreciate you pushing on that, I've heard stories of the title changing and the comp lagging by two quarters.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: I'm aware of those stories too, which is exactly why I want to flag it up front rather than assume it'll happen on its own.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: I'll keep you posted as it moves through review.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Thanks, that helps me plan, I was half-holding off on some personal stuff pending how this quarter shakes out.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Fair enough, I don't want to overpromise a date, but I do want you to know I'm actually pushing this, not just nodding along in the meeting.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: I believe you, you've followed through on stuff like this before, that's part of why I brought it up today instead of just quietly hoping someone noticed.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Good, I'd rather you bring things up directly.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Switching gears completely, anything going on outside work worth mentioning?

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: You mentioned the conference earlier.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Not much, mostly just trying to get outside more now that it's cooling off, I've been doing some trail running on weekends, which is a nice contrast to staring at calibration curves all week.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: That sounds like a good reset.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Any races on the calendar, or just for fun?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Just for fun for now, though a few people at the running club keep trying to talk me into a half marathon in the spring, which would line up annoyingly well with the Aegis launch.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Sounds like March is shaping up to be a competitive month between that and the conference.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: We'll figure out the calendar together so you're not choosing between them at the last minute.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Appreciated.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Speaking of the launch date, is it still firm after yesterday's discussion, or is that something we're still watching?

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: As far as I know it's still firm, Sun's been pretty protective of the date given the trade show it's tied to, even with Rafael's tooling concerns.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: That's the enclosure tooling, right, the anodized aluminum housing?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: I heard there was some back and forth with the supplier about mold revisions.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Yeah, Rafael's got a call with them tomorrow afternoon actually, I think it's around the same time as your call today, funnily enough, different building though.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Small world.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: I hope his goes better than the last one, I heard the first batch of enclosures had some finish issues.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: That's my understanding too, we'll see what comes out of today's call.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: If the tooling slips it could ripple into your firmware timeline as well, since the enclosure has the antenna cutout for the Bluetooth module.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Right, I already flagged that to Tomas and Inès a few minutes ago, we calibrated the antenna matching against the current enclosure prototype, so any geometry change is worth knowing about early.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Good, glad that's already moving.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Send me a one-line summary after your call today, I'll fold it into my notes for Sun.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Will do.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Appreciated, I'll take it one quarter at a time.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Okay, I should actually wrap up, the supplier call is in a few minutes and I want to reread their last email first.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Go ahead, one last thing though, anything you need from me right now, blockers, decisions, anything at all?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Not urgently.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Maybe just backup on the Rafael dependency if that yield data doesn't show up by Wednesday.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Will do, ping me and I'll shake it loose.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: This was a good conversation, thanks for being direct about the lead role thing, I think it's the right move for you and for the team.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Thanks for listening, and for the feedback.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: I'll get you that proposal by Friday, documentation plan included.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Sounds good.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Good luck with the supplier call.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Thanks, talk later.

summary_markdown:
## Key decisions

- Maya will draft a proposal for a formal firmware team-lead role covering the Vantage line (and eventually Aegis), including a staffing plan, a time-split between leading and doing, a ramp plan for Greta, and a plan to document the calibration pipeline as she delegates pieces of it.
- The corrected calibration lookup table validation will be handed to Greta to run, with Maya reviewing the data and owning the ship decision — a first concrete step toward the lead role.
- A short incident write-up on the humidity-drift root cause will be added to the incident log once the soak test finishes.
- The owner will push to keep a title change and the associated comp review in the same review cycle rather than sequential.

## Discussion

Maya reported finding the root cause of the humidity-channel drift Solenne Biolabs flagged: a reference temperature compensation table built off an outdated thermistor curve. A corrected table is ready and will go through a 72-hour, three-setpoint soak test on twelve bench units, targeting a patch ahead of the main Q4 release. The conversation moved to Maya's career direction: she wants to move from individual-contributor work toward leading the sensor firmware team, mentoring Inès and Greta and owning the roadmap rather than only executing it. The owner gave positive feedback on Q3 (the August calibration accuracy work, and steady handling of the team), with one growth area flagged — getting more of Maya's calibration-pipeline knowledge out of her head and into documentation, partly as risk mitigation and partly to make delegation easier as she takes on more of a lead role. They also discussed workload (busy but not burnt out; a spring sensor conference penciled in), Greta's onboarding (good instincts, would benefit from seeing a full calibration cycle end to end, and a smaller first project for future hires), the enclosure supplier's tooling lead time and its knock-on risk to BLE antenna range testing, and logistics for how a lead-role title change and comp conversation would move through review.

## Action items

Maya will draft the firmware lead-role proposal, covering staffing, time-split, Greta's ramp plan, and a documentation plan, by next Friday.

## Open questions

- Whether the Aegis launch date holds given the enclosure tooling lead-time risk Rafael raised at steerco.
- Whether Rafael's manufacturing team's bandwidth constraints become a recurring blocker before the Aegis launch.
- How quickly title and comp review can move through leadership once Maya's proposal is submitted.
notes_markdown:
- Calibration drift root cause found: stale thermistor curve, not a sensor defect — corrected table in soak test, Greta running validation
- Maya wants a formal firmware lead role (Vantage now, Aegis later); asked her for a written proposal by next Friday
- Feedback given: strong Q3 (calibration accuracy, steady team handling); growth area = document the calibration pipeline
- Greta ramp: needs exposure to a full calibration cycle end to end, not just her current slice
- Push comp review to follow title change in the same cycle, not months later
- Enclosure tooling lead time (Rafael, steerco) could affect BLE antenna range testing — flagged to Tomas/Inès

action_items.description: Draft a proposal for a formal firmware team-lead role: staffing, time-split between leading and doing, Greta's ramp plan, and a plan to document the calibration pipeline while delegating.
